Continuous Time Autocorrelation Function (ctACF)

Source: R/ctACF.R
ctACF.Rd

Computes autocorrelations and cross correlations by time lag, pooled over subjects, for data observed at irregular times.

Usage

ctACF(
  dat,
  varnames = "auto",
  ccfnames = "all",
  idcol = "id",
  timecol = "time",
  plot = TRUE,
  timestep = "auto",
  time.max = "auto",
  nboot = 100,
  scale = FALSE,
  center = FALSE
)

Arguments

dat

The input data in data frame or data table format, in long format.

varnames

Character vector of variable names in the data to compute the ACF for. 'auto' uses all columns that are not time / id.

ccfnames

Character vector of variable names in the data to compute cross correlation for. 'all' uses all variables in varnames, NA uses none.

idcol

The name of the column containing subject IDs (default is 'id').

timecol

The name of the column containing time values (default is 'time').

plot

A logical value indicating whether to create a plot (default is TRUE).

timestep

The width of the time lag bins. 'auto' (default) uses half the median time interval between consecutive rows of a subject.

time.max

The largest time lag to compute. 'auto' (default) uses two thirds of the mean, over rows, of the time span of the row's subject.

nboot

The number of bootstrap samples, each resampling subjects with replacement (default is 100).

scale

if TRUE, divide each variable by its within-subject standard deviation.

center

if TRUE, subtract each variable's within-subject mean.

Value

If 'plot' is TRUE, the function returns a ggplot object of the ACF plot. If 'plot' is FALSE, it returns a data table with a row for each sample, variable and time lag: Sample (0 for the data, then the bootstrap samples), ACF, TimeInterval, Variable, SignificanceLevel (the 95% bound of a correlation of zero computed from that many independent pairs), and Pairs, the number of pairs the correlation is computed from.

Details

Within each subject, every pair of observations is put in the time lag bin nearest to the time between them, at multiples of timestep up to time.max. The value at a lag is the correlation of the pairs in its bin, pooled over subjects. For an autocorrelation this is a variable at time t + lag with the same variable at time t. For the cross correlation 'x_y' it is x at time t + lag with y at time t, so at a positive lag y is the earlier. Lags with fewer than three pairs are left out. Autocorrelations are returned from the first non-zero lag, as the lag 0 autocorrelation is always 1. Cross correlations include lag 0, the contemporaneous correlation. Bootstrap samples resample whole subjects, and the plot shows a spline through the estimates with a band from their bootstrap spread (see plotctACF).

Examples

data.table::setDTthreads(1) #ignore this line
# Example usage:
head(ctstantestdat)
ctACF(ctstantestdat,varnames=c('Y1'),idcol='id',timecol='time',nboot=5)
